TheoreticalMechanics/en/57.response:
\[
S_{2}(p,Q,t)=-\tan p\;(e^{Q}-1)\qquad\text{(type‑2 generating function)}
\]

From a type‑2 generating function we have  

\[
q=\frac{\partial S_{2}}{\partial p},\qquad 
P=-\frac{\partial S_{2}}{\partial Q}\; .
\]

Hence  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
q &=\frac{\partial}{\partial p}\Big[-\tan p\,(e^{Q}-1)\Big]
   =-(e^{Q}-1)\sec^{2}p ,\\[4pt]
P &=-\frac{\partial}{\partial Q}\Big[-\tan p\,(e^{Q}-1)\Big]
   =\;e^{Q}\tan p .
\end{aligned}}
\]

The transformation can be written explicitly in either direction.  

**Inverse (new → old) form:**  

\[
p=\arctan\!\big(Pe^{-Q}\big),\qquad 
q=-(e^{Q}-1)\Big[1+P^{2}e^{-2Q}\Big] .
\]

Thus the canonical map \((p,q)\mapsto (P,Q)\) is defined implicitly by  

\[
P=e^{Q}\tan p ,\qquad 
q=-(e^{Q}-1)\sec^{2}p ,
\]

or equivalently by the explicit expressions above.  (Since \(S_{2}\) has no explicit time dependence, the new Hamiltonian is \(K=H+\partial S_{2}/\partial t=H\).)

QuantumMechanics/en/357.response:
The Zeeman interaction of a single‑electron atom in a weak magnetic field \(\mathbf B = B\hat z\) is  

\[
\hat H'=\mu_{B}(\mathbf L+g_{s}\mathbf S)\cdot\mathbf B
       =\mu_{B}B\,(L_{z}+2S_{z})\qquad(g_{s}\simeq2).
\]

In the fine–structure basis \(|n\ell s jm_{j}\rangle\) (LS coupling) the first‑order energy correction is  

\[
\Delta E^{(1)}_{jm_{j}}
    =\langle n\ell s jm_{j}|\hat H'|n\ell s jm_{j}\rangle .
\]

Because \(\mathbf J=\mathbf L+\mathbf S\) is the only vector that survives in the expectation value,  

\[
\langle\mathbf L\rangle=\frac{\langle\mathbf L\!\cdot\!\mathbf J\rangle}
                              {j(j+1)}\langle\mathbf J\rangle ,\qquad
\langle\mathbf S\rangle=\frac{\langle\mathbf S\!\cdot\!\mathbf J\rangle}
                              {j(j+1)}\langle\mathbf J\rangle .
\]

Using  

\[
\mathbf L\!\cdot\!\mathbf J=\tfrac12\bigl[J^{2}+L^{2}-S^{2}\bigr],
\qquad 
\mathbf S\!\cdot\!\mathbf J=\tfrac12\bigl[J^{2}-L^{2}+S^{2}\bigr],
\]

and the eigenvalues \(L^{2}=\ell(\ell+1)\hbar^{2}\), \(S^{2}=s(s+1)\hbar^{2}\), \(J^{2}=j(j+1)\hbar^{2}\), we obtain  

\[
\langle L_{z}\rangle=\frac{j(j+1)+\ell(\ell+1)-s(s+1)}{2j(j+1)}\,m_{j}\hbar,
\]
\[
\langle S_{z}\rangle=\frac{j(j+1)-\ell(\ell+1)+s(s+1)}{2j(j+1)}\,m_{j}\hbar .
\]

Therefore  

\[
\Delta E^{(1)}_{jm_{j}}
= \mu_{B}B\bigl(\langle L_{z}\rangle+2\langle S_{z}\rangle\bigr)
= \mu_{B}B\;g_{j}\,m_{j},
\]

with the Landé factor  

\[
g_{j}=1+\frac{j(j+1)+s(s+1)-\ell(\ell+1)}{2j(j+1)} .
\]

For a p‑electron (\(\ell=1\)) and an electron spin (\(s=\tfrac12\)) the state with  
\(j=\tfrac32\) gives  

\[
g_{j=\frac32}=1+\frac{\frac{15}{4}+\frac34-2}{2\cdot\frac{15}{4}}
               =\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\Delta E^{(1)}_{j=\frac32,m_{j}}
    =\frac{4}{3}\,\mu_{B}B\,m_{j}
    =\frac{4}{3}\,\varepsilon\,m_{j},
\qquad\varepsilon\equiv\mu_{B}B\ll W .
\]

For the possible magnetic quantum numbers \(m_{j}=3/2,\;1/2,\;-1/2,\;-3/2\) we obtain the four Zeeman shifts:

\[
\boxed{
\Delta E_{j=\frac32,m_j}=g_{j=\frac32}\,\varepsilon\,m_j
   =\frac{4}{3}\,\varepsilon\,m_j
   =\begin{cases}
      2\varepsilon & m_j=\tfrac{3}{2},\\[4pt]
      \frac{2}{3}\varepsilon & m_j=\tfrac{1}{2},\\[4pt]
      -\frac{2}{3}\varepsilon & m_j=-\tfrac{1}{2},\\[4pt]
      -2\varepsilon & m_j=-\tfrac{3}{2}.
     \end{cases}
}
\] 

These are the first‑order Zeeman energy changes for the \(j=\frac32\) manifold of a single‑electron atom with \(\ell=1\) in a weak magnetic field.
